concepts.name: Set notation and membership
concepts.summary: Read and write sets using roster and set-builder notation and decide whether an element belongs to a set or a set is a subset of another.

concepts.name: Set operations and Venn diagrams
concepts.summary: Compute and explain union, intersection, difference and complement and represent them with Venn diagrams.

concepts.name: Propositions and logical connectives
concepts.summary: Identify statements that are true or false and explain the meaning of AND, OR, NOT, implication and biconditional.

concepts.name: Truth tables
concepts.summary: Build a truth table for a compound proposition and read off when it is true or false.

concepts.name: Functions as mappings
concepts.summary: Explain a function as a rule assigning each domain element exactly one codomain element, distinguishing domain, codomain and range.

concepts.name: Counting by sum and product
concepts.summary: Explain when to add and when to multiply counts of choices in simple counting problems.

misconceptions.text: The empty set and the set containing the empty set are the same thing.
The implication 'if P then Q' is false whenever P is false.
In ordinary logic, 'or' means exactly one of the two is true.

concepts.name: Logical equivalence and De Morgan
concepts.summary: Apply equivalences such as De Morgan's laws and the contrapositive to rewrite statements and recognize tautologies and contradictions.

concepts.name: Quantifiers and negation
concepts.summary: Translate statements into predicates with for-all and there-exists and correctly negate them.

concepts.name: Relations and their properties
concepts.summary: Represent relations as sets of pairs and test them for reflexivity, symmetry, antisymmetry and transitivity.

concepts.name: Injective, surjective and bijective functions
concepts.summary: Classify functions as one-to-one, onto or both and use composition and inverses of bijections.

concepts.name: Permutations and combinations
concepts.summary: Compute counts of ordered and unordered selections with and without repetition and choose the right formula.

concepts.name: Direct proof
concepts.summary: Write a direct proof of a simple statement from definitions, such as properties of even and odd integers.

concepts.name: Divisibility and modular congruence
concepts.summary: Use divisibility, remainders and congruence mod n to compute sums, products and powers of residues.

misconceptions.text: The negation of 'for all x, P(x)' is 'for all x, not P(x)'.
A relation that is symmetric and transitive must also be reflexive.
Order matters in combinations just as it does in permutations.

concepts.name: Proof by contradiction and contrapositive
concepts.summary: Choose and carry out contrapositive or contradiction proofs, such as irrationality of the square root of 2.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction
concepts.summary: Prove statements over the natural numbers with a base case and an inductive step using the inductive hypothesis.

concepts.name: Strong induction
concepts.summary: Decide when strong induction is needed and use several earlier cases in the inductive step.

concepts.name: Equivalence relations and partitions
concepts.summary: Analyse how an equivalence relation splits a set into classes and connect it to partitions, including congruence classes.

concepts.name: Inclusion-exclusion principle
concepts.summary: Count elements of unions of overlapping sets by alternating sums of intersection sizes.

concepts.name: Pigeonhole principle
concepts.summary: Identify the pigeons and holes in a problem and apply basic and generalized pigeonhole arguments.

concepts.name: Solving linear recurrences
concepts.summary: Set up recurrences from problems and solve first-order and linear homogeneous second-order ones by iteration or characteristic roots.

concepts.name: Modular inverses and the Euclidean algorithm
concepts.summary: Compute gcds and modular inverses and solve linear congruences.

misconceptions.text: In an induction proof, the inductive step may assume the statement for all n, including the one being proved.
The base case is a formality and can be skipped when the inductive step works.
The pigeonhole principle tells you which hole holds multiple pigeons.

concepts.name: Nested quantifiers and proof strategy
concepts.summary: Analyse how the order of nested quantifiers changes meaning and pick proof strategies for statements with several quantifiers.

concepts.name: Structural induction
concepts.summary: Prove properties of recursively defined sets, strings and trees by induction over their construction.

concepts.name: Generating functions for counting
concepts.summary: Use generating functions to count selections with constraints and to solve recurrences, judging when they beat direct methods.

concepts.name: Non-homogeneous recurrences and divide-and-conquer
concepts.summary: Solve recurrences with forcing terms and evaluate solution methods for divide-and-conquer cost recurrences.

concepts.name: Binomial identities and combinatorial proof
concepts.summary: Establish identities by counting one set in two ways or by building a bijection, and compare with algebraic proofs.

concepts.name: Cardinality and countability
concepts.summary: Compare sizes of sets via bijections, show sets are countable, and use the diagonal argument to show uncountability.

concepts.name: Number-theoretic theorems and applications
concepts.summary: Apply Fermat, Euler and the Chinese remainder theorem and evaluate their use in modular computation and RSA-style cryptography.

concepts.name: Partial orders and lattices
concepts.summary: Analyse partial orders using Hasse diagrams, extremal elements, chains and antichains.

misconceptions.text: For all x there exists y is logically the same as there exists y for all x.
All infinite sets have the same size.
Fermat's little theorem holds for any modulus, not only primes.

concepts.name: Formal proof design and evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge the validity, rigour and elegance of proofs, spot subtle flaws, and select the most suitable technique for a new claim.

concepts.name: Asymptotic analysis of recurrences
concepts.summary: Derive and justify tight bounds for irregular recurrences and compare methods such as substitution, recursion trees and generating functions.

concepts.name: Probabilistic and extremal methods
concepts.summary: Design existence arguments using expected values or extremal choices to prove combinatorial results without construction.

concepts.name: Generalized pigeonhole and Ramsey theory
concepts.summary: Evaluate Ramsey-type guarantees of structure in large systems and construct arguments or bounds for small cases.

concepts.name: Inclusion-exclusion with Möbius inversion
concepts.summary: Generalize inclusion-exclusion to posets and use it for derangements, sieve counts and inversion formulas.

concepts.name: Formal logic and decidability limits
concepts.summary: Evaluate the expressive power and limits of propositional and first-order logic, including satisfiability, completeness and undecidability.

concepts.name: Modelling problems discretely
concepts.summary: Create discrete models of real problems by choosing sets, relations, recurrences or counting structures and justify the choice.

misconceptions.text: A probabilistic existence proof gives an efficient way to construct the object.
Ramsey numbers are easy to compute exactly once the general bounds are known.
Any true statement in first-order arithmetic can be proven from a fixed axiom system.
